title: Measurability of membership disagreement
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\Xi$ be measurable spaces, let $A\subseteq\Xi$ be measurable, and let $f,g:\Omega\to\Xi$ be measurable maps. Then the set of $z\in\Omega$ for which exactly one of $f(z)$ and $g(z)$ belongs to $A$ is measurable.
replaced: Let $\Omega,\Xi$ be measurable spaces, $A\subseteq\Xi$ a measurable set, and $f,g:\Omega\to\Xi$ measurable maps. Then $\{z:\neg(f(z)\in A\ \Longleftrightarrow\ g(z)\in A)\}$ is measurable.
